00362:  * written to the Database together. Each child property can either be a simple
00363:  * property (for example, "name") or a relative path (for example,
00364:  * "name/first") from the current location to the data to update.
00365:  *
00366:  * As opposed to the `set()` method, `update()` can be use to selectively update
00367:  * only the referenced properties at the current location (instead of replacing
00368:  * all the child properties at the current location).
00369:  *
00370:  * The effect of the write will be visible immediately, and the corresponding
00371:  * events ('value', 'child_added', etc.) will be triggered. Synchronization of
00372:  * the data to the Firebase servers will also be started, and the returned
00373:  * Promise will resolve when complete. If provided, the `onComplete` callback
00374:  * will be called asynchronously after synchronization has finished.
00375:  *
00376:  * A single `update()` will generate a single "value" event at the location
00377:  * where the `update()` was performed, regardless of how many children were
00378:  * modified.
00379:  *
00380:  * Note that modifying data with `update()` will cancel any pending
00381:  * transactions at that location, so extreme care should be taken if mixing

00031: /**
00032:  * SyncTree is the central class for managing event callback registration, data caching, views
00033:  * (query processing), and event generation.  There are typically two SyncTree instances for
00034:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
00035:  *
00036:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
00037:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
00038:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
00039:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
00040:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
00041:  *    applyServerMerge()).
00042:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
00043:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
00044:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
00045:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
00046:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
00047:  *
00048:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
00049:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
00050:  *
00051:  */
00052: export declare class SyncTree {
00053:     listenProvider_: ListenProvider;
-------------------------------------------------------------
00051:  */

07603: class ImmutableTree {
07604:     static fromObject(obj) {
07605:         let tree = new ImmutableTree(null);
07606:         each(obj, (childPath, childSnap) => {
07607:             tree = tree.set(new Path(childPath), childSnap);
07608:         });
07609:         return tree;
07610:     }
07611:     constructor(value, children = EmptyChildren()) {
07612:         this.value = value;
07613:         this.children = children;
07614:     }
07615:     /**
07616:      * True if the value is empty and there are no children
07617:      */
07618:     isEmpty() {
07619:         return this.value === null && this.children.isEmpty();
07620:     }
07621:     /**
07622:      * Given a path and predicate, return the first node and the path to that node
-------------------------------------------------------------
07689:      */
07690:     set(relativePath, toSet) {
07691:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
07692:             return new ImmutableTree(toSet, this.children);
07693:         }
07694:         else {
07695:             const front = pathGetFront(relativePath);
07696:             const child = this.children.get(front) || new ImmutableTree(null);
07697:             const newChild = child.set(pathPopFront(relativePath), toSet);
07698:             const newChildren = this.children.insert(front, newChild);
07699:             return new ImmutableTree(this.value, newChildren);
07700:         }
07701:     }
07702:     /**
07703:      * Removes the value at the specified path.
07704:      *
07705:      * @param relativePath - Path to value to remove.
07706:      * @returns Resulting tree.
07707:      */
07708:     remove(relativePath) {
07709:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
07710:             if (this.children.isEmpty()) {
07711:                 return new ImmutableTree(null);
07712:             }

07912:     }

07915:         if (rootmost != null) {

09506:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
09507:  *
09508:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
09509:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
09510:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
09511:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
09512:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
09513:  *    applyServerMerge()).
09514:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
09515:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
09516:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
09517:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
09518:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
09519:  *
09520:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
09521:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
09522:  *
09523:  */
09524: class SyncTree {

09528:      */

11244: function repoCallOnCompleteCallback(repo, callback, status, errorReason) {

11246:         exceptionGuard(() => {

11249:             }

11255:                 }
11256:                 const error = new Error(message);
11257:                 // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any

11259:                 callback(error);

00030: export declare function resetSyncTreeTag(): void;
00031: /**
00032:  * SyncTree is the central class for managing event callback registration, data caching, views
00033:  * (query processing), and event generation.  There are typically two SyncTree instances for
00034:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
00035:  *
00036:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
00037:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
00038:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
00039:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
00040:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
00041:  *    applyServerMerge()).
00042:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
00043:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
00044:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
00045:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
00046:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
00047:  *
00048:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
00049:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
00050:  *
00051:  */
00052: export declare class SyncTree {
00053:     listenProvider_: ListenProvider;
-------------------------------------------------------------
00051:  */
00052: export declare class SyncTree {
00053:     listenProvider_: ListenProvider;
00054:     /**
00055:      * Tree of SyncPoints.  There's a SyncPoint at any location that has 1 or more views.
00056:      */
00057:     syncPointTree_: ImmutableTree<SyncPoint>;
00058:     /**
00059:      * A tree of all pending user writes (user-initiated set()'s, transaction()'s, update()'s, etc.).
00060:      */
00061:     pendingWriteTree_: WriteTree;
00062:     readonly tagToQueryMap: Map<number, string>;
00063:     readonly queryToTagMap: Map<string, number>;
00064:     /**
00065:      * @param listenProvider_ - Used by SyncTree to start / stop listening
00066:      *   to server data.

07603: class ImmutableTree {
07604:     static fromObject(obj) {
07605:         let tree = new ImmutableTree(null);
07606:         each(obj, (childPath, childSnap) => {
07607:             tree = tree.set(new Path(childPath), childSnap);
07608:         });

07610:     }
07611:     constructor(value, children = EmptyChildren()) {
07612:         this.value = value;
07613:         this.children = children;
07614:     }
07615:     /**
07616:      * True if the value is empty and there are no children
07617:      */
07618:     isEmpty() {
07619:         return this.value === null && this.children.isEmpty();
07620:     }
07621:     /**
07622:      * Given a path and predicate, return the first node and the path to that node
-------------------------------------------------------------
07689:      */
07690:     set(relativePath, toSet) {
07691:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
07692:             return new ImmutableTree(toSet, this.children);
07693:         }
07694:         else {
07695:             const front = pathGetFront(relativePath);
07696:             const child = this.children.get(front) || new ImmutableTree(null);
07697:             const newChild = child.set(pathPopFront(relativePath), toSet);
07698:             const newChildren = this.children.insert(front, newChild);
07699:             return new ImmutableTree(this.value, newChildren);
07700:         }
07701:     }
07702:     /**
07703:      * Removes the value at the specified path.
07704:      *
07705:      * @param relativePath - Path to value to remove.
07706:      * @returns Resulting tree.
07707:      */
07708:     remove(relativePath) {
07709:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
07710:             if (this.children.isEmpty()) {
07711:                 return new ImmutableTree(null);
07712:             }

07912:     }
07913:     else {
07914:         const rootmost = compoundWrite.writeTree_.findRootMostValueAndPath(path);
07915:         if (rootmost != null) {
07916:             const rootMostPath = rootmost.path;
07917:             let value = rootmost.value;
07918:             const relativePath = newRelativePath(rootMostPath, path);
07919:             value = value.updateChild(relativePath, node);
07920:             return new CompoundWrite(compoundWrite.writeTree_.set(rootMostPath, value));
07921:         }
07922:         else {
07923:             const subtree = new ImmutableTree(node);
07924:             const newWriteTree = compoundWrite.writeTree_.setTree(path, subtree);
07925:             return new CompoundWrite(newWriteTree);
07926:         }

09502: let syncTreeNextQueryTag_ = 1;
09503: /**
09504:  * SyncTree is the central class for managing event callback registration, data caching, views
09505:  * (query processing), and event generation.  There are typically two SyncTree instances for
09506:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
09507:  *
09508:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
09509:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
09510:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
09511:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
09512:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
09513:  *    applyServerMerge()).
09514:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
09515:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
09516:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
09517:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
09518:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
09519:  *
09520:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
09521:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
09522:  *
09523:  */

12799:  *
12800:  * Note that modifying data with `update()` will cancel any pending
12801:  * transactions at that location, so extreme care should be taken if mixing
12802:  * `update()` and `transaction()` to modify the same data.
12803:  *
12804:  * Passing `null` to `update()` will remove the data at this location.
12805:  *
12806:  * See
12807:  * {@link https://firebase.googleblog.com/2015/09/introducing-multi-location-updates-and_86.html | Introducing multi-location updates and more}.
12808:  *
12809:  * @param ref - The location to write to.
12810:  * @param values - Object containing multiple values.
12811:  * @returns Resolves when update on server is complete.
12812:  */

09498: let syncTreeNextQueryTag_ = 1;
09499: /**
09500:  * SyncTree is the central class for managing event callback registration, data caching, views
09501:  * (query processing), and event generation.  There are typically two SyncTree instances for
09502:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
09503:  *
09504:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
09505:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
09506:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
09507:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
09508:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
09509:  *    applyServerMerge()).
09510:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
09511:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
09512:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
09513:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
09514:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
09515:  *
09516:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
09517:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
09518:  *
09519:  */
09520: class SyncTree {

09939: function syncTreeCreateListenerForView_(syncTree, view) {
09940:     const query = view.query;
09941:     const tag = syncTreeTagForQuery(syncTree, query);
09942:     return {
09943:         hashFn: () => {
09944:             const cache = viewGetServerCache(view) || ChildrenNode.EMPTY_NODE;
09945:             return cache.hash();
09946:         },
09947:         onComplete: (status) => {
09948:             if (status === 'ok') {
09949:                 if (tag) {
09950:                     return syncTreeApplyTaggedListenComplete(syncTree, query._path, tag);
09951:                 }
09952:                 else {
09953:                     return syncTreeApplyListenComplete(syncTree, query._path);
09954:                 }
09955:             }
09956:             else {
09957:                 // If a listen failed, kill all of the listeners here, not just the one that triggered the error.

11647:         repoPruneCompletedTransactionsBelowNode(repo, childNode);

07611: class ImmutableTree {
07612:     static fromObject(obj) {
07613:         let tree = new ImmutableTree(null);
07614:         each(obj, (childPath, childSnap) => {
07615:             tree = tree.set(new Path(childPath), childSnap);
07616:         });
07617:         return tree;
07618:     }
07619:     constructor(value, children = EmptyChildren()) {
07620:         this.value = value;
07621:         this.children = children;
07622:     }
07623:     /**
07624:      * True if the value is empty and there are no children
07625:      */
07626:     isEmpty() {
07627:         return this.value === null && this.children.isEmpty();
07628:     }
07629:     /**
07630:      * Given a path and predicate, return the first node and the path to that node
-------------------------------------------------------------
07697:      */
07698:     set(relativePath, toSet) {
07699:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
07700:             return new ImmutableTree(toSet, this.children);
07701:         }
07702:         else {
07703:             const front = pathGetFront(relativePath);
07704:             const child = this.children.get(front) || new ImmutableTree(null);
07705:             const newChild = child.set(pathPopFront(relativePath), toSet);
07706:             const newChildren = this.children.insert(front, newChild);
07707:             return new ImmutableTree(this.value, newChildren);
07708:         }
07709:     }

09510: let syncTreeNextQueryTag_ = 1;
09511: /**
09512:  * SyncTree is the central class for managing event callback registration, data caching, views
09513:  * (query processing), and event generation.  There are typically two SyncTree instances for
09514:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
09515:  *
09516:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
09517:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
09518:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
09519:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
09520:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
09521:  *    applyServerMerge()).
09522:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
09523:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
09524:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
09525:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
09526:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
09527:  *
09528:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
09529:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
09530:  *
09531:  */
09532: class SyncTree {
09533:     /**
-------------------------------------------------------------
09536:      */
09537:     constructor(listenProvider_) {
09538:         this.listenProvider_ = listenProvider_;
09539:         /**
09540:          * Tree of SyncPoints.  There's a SyncPoint at any location that has 1 or more views.
09541:          */

09543:         /**
09544:          * A tree of all pending user writes (user-initiated set()'s, transaction()'s, update()'s, etc.).
09545:          */
09546:         this.pendingWriteTree_ = newWriteTree();
09547:         this.tagToQueryMap = new Map();
09548:         this.queryToTagMap = new Map();
09549:     }
09550: }

11245: function repoLog(repo, ...varArgs) {
11246:     let prefix = '';
11247:     if (repo.persistentConnection_) {
11248:         prefix = repo.persistentConnection_.id + ':';
11249:     }
11250:     log(prefix, ...varArgs);

11252: function repoCallOnCompleteCallback(repo, callback, status, errorReason) {
11253:     if (callback) {
11254:         exceptionGuard(() => {
11255:             if (status === 'ok') {
11256:                 callback(null);
11257:             }
11258:             else {
11259:                 const code = (status || 'error').toUpperCase();
11260:                 let message = code;
11261:                 if (errorReason) {
11262:                     message += ': ' + errorReason;
11263:                 }
11264:                 const error = new Error(message);
11265:                 // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
11266:                 error.code = code;
11267:                 callback(error);
-------------------------------------------------------------
11247:     if (repo.persistentConnection_) {
11248:         prefix = repo.persistentConnection_.id + ':';
11249:     }
11250:     log(prefix, ...varArgs);
11251: }

11252: function repoCallOnCompleteCallback(repo, callback, status, errorReason) {
11253:     if (callback) {
11254:         exceptionGuard(() => {
11255:             if (status === 'ok') {
11256:                 callback(null);
11257:             }
11258:             else {
11259:                 const code = (status || 'error').toUpperCase();
11260:                 let message = code;
11261:                 if (errorReason) {
11262:                     message += ': ' + errorReason;
11263:                 }
11264:                 const error = new Error(message);
11265:                 // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
11266:                 error.code = code;
11267:                 callback(error);
11268:             }
11269:         });
11270:     }

07605: /**
07606:  * A tree with immutable elements.
07607:  */
07608: class ImmutableTree {
07609:     static fromObject(obj) {
07610:         let tree = new ImmutableTree(null);
07611:         each(obj, (childPath, childSnap) => {
07612:             tree = tree.set(new Path(childPath), childSnap);
07613:         });
07614:         return tree;
07615:     }
07616:     constructor(value, children = EmptyChildren()) {
07617:         this.value = value;
07618:         this.children = children;
07619:     }
07620:     /**
07621:      * True if the value is empty and there are no children
07622:      */
07623:     isEmpty() {
07624:         return this.value === null && this.children.isEmpty();
07625:     }
07626:     /**
07627:      * Given a path and predicate, return the first node and the path to that node
-------------------------------------------------------------
07694:      */
07695:     set(relativePath, toSet) {
07696:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
07697:             return new ImmutableTree(toSet, this.children);
07698:         }
07699:         else {
07700:             const front = pathGetFront(relativePath);
07701:             const child = this.children.get(front) || new ImmutableTree(null);
07702:             const newChild = child.set(pathPopFront(relativePath), toSet);
07703:             const newChildren = this.children.insert(front, newChild);
07704:             return new ImmutableTree(this.value, newChildren);
07705:         }
07706:     }
07707:     /**
07708:      * Removes the value at the specified path.
07709:      *
07710:      * @param relativePath - Path to value to remove.
07711:      * @returns Resulting tree.
07712:      */
07713:     remove(relativePath) {
07714:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
07715:             if (this.children.isEmpty()) {
07716:                 return new ImmutableTree(null);
07717:             }

07920:         if (rootmost != null) {

07930:             return new CompoundWrite(newWriteTree);
07931:         }

09508: /**
09509:  * SyncTree is the central class for managing event callback registration, data caching, views
09510:  * (query processing), and event generation.  There are typically two SyncTree instances for
09511:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
09512:  *
09513:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
09514:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
09515:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
09516:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
09517:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
09518:  *    applyServerMerge()).
09519:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
09520:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
09521:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
09522:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
09523:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
09524:  *
09525:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
09526:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
09527:  *
09528:  */

09530:     /**

09533:      */

11249: function repoCallOnCompleteCallback(repo, callback, status, errorReason) {
11250:     if (callback) {
11251:         exceptionGuard(() => {
11252:             if (status === 'ok') {
11253:                 callback(null);
11254:             }
11255:             else {
11256:                 const code = (status || 'error').toUpperCase();
11257:                 let message = code;
11258:                 if (errorReason) {
11259:                     message += ': ' + errorReason;
11260:                 }
11261:                 const error = new Error(message);
11262:                 // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
11263:                 error.code = code;
11264:                 callback(error);

02613:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
02614:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
02615:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
02616:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
02617:  *    applyServerMerge()).
02618:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
02619:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
02620:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
02621:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
02622:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
02623:  *
02624:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
02625:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.

12529: class ImmutableTree {
12530:     static fromObject(obj) {
12531:         let tree = new ImmutableTree(null);
12532:         each(obj, (childPath, childSnap) => {
12533:             tree = tree.set(new Path(childPath), childSnap);
12534:         });
12535:         return tree;
12536:     }
12537:     constructor(value, children = EmptyChildren()) {
12538:         this.value = value;
12539:         this.children = children;
12540:     }
12541:     /**
12542:      * True if the value is empty and there are no children
12543:      */
12544:     isEmpty() {
12545:         return this.value === null && this.children.isEmpty();
12546:     }
12547:     /**
12548:      * Given a path and predicate, return the first node and the path to that node
-------------------------------------------------------------
12615:      */
12616:     set(relativePath, toSet) {
12617:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
12618:             return new ImmutableTree(toSet, this.children);
12619:         }
12620:         else {
12621:             const front = pathGetFront(relativePath);
12622:             const child = this.children.get(front) || new ImmutableTree(null);
12623:             const newChild = child.set(pathPopFront(relativePath), toSet);
12624:             const newChildren = this.children.insert(front, newChild);
12625:             return new ImmutableTree(this.value, newChildren);
12626:         }
12627:     }
12628:     /**
12629:      * Removes the value at the specified path.
12630:      *
12631:      * @param relativePath - Path to value to remove.
12632:      * @returns Resulting tree.
12633:      */
12634:     remove(relativePath) {
12635:         if (pathIsEmpty(relativePath)) {
12636:             if (this.children.isEmpty()) {
12637:                 return new ImmutableTree(null);
12638:             }

14429: /**
14430:  * SyncTree is the central class for managing event callback registration, data caching, views
14431:  * (query processing), and event generation.  There are typically two SyncTree instances for
14432:  * each Repo, one for the normal Firebase data, and one for the .info data.
14433:  *
14434:  * It has a number of responsibilities, including:
14435:  *  - Tracking all user event callbacks (registered via addEventRegistration() and removeEventRegistration()).
14436:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for user set(), transaction(), and update() calls
14437:  *    (applyUserOverwrite(), applyUserMerge()).
14438:  *  - Applying and caching data changes for server data changes (applyServerOverwrite(),
14439:  *    applyServerMerge()).
14440:  *  - Generating user-facing events for server and user changes (all of the apply* methods
14441:  *    return the set of events that need to be raised as a result).
14442:  *  - Maintaining the appropriate set of server listens to ensure we are always subscribed
14443:  *    to the correct set of paths and queries to satisfy the current set of user event
14444:  *    callbacks (listens are started/stopped using the provided listenProvider).
14445:  *
14446:  * NOTE: Although SyncTree tracks event callbacks and calculates events to raise, the actual
14447:  * events are returned to the caller rather than raised synchronously.
14448:  *
14449:  */
14450: class SyncTree {
14451:     /**
-------------------------------------------------------------
14454:      */

14456:         this.listenProvider_ = listenProvider_;
14457:         /**
14458:          * Tree of SyncPoints.  There's a SyncPoint at any location that has 1 or more views.
14459:          */
14460:         this.syncPointTree_ = new ImmutableTree(null);
14461:         /**
14462:          * A tree of all pending user writes (user-initiated set()'s, transaction()'s, update()'s, etc.).
14463:          */
14464:         this.pendingWriteTree_ = newWriteTree();
14465:         this.tagToQueryMap = new Map();
14466:         this.queryToTagMap = new Map();
14467:     }
14468: }

16292: function repoSendReadyTransactions(repo, node = repo.transactionQueueTree_) {
16293:     // Before recursing, make sure any completed transactions are removed.
16294:     if (!node) {
16295:         repoPruneCompletedTransactionsBelowNode(repo, node);
16296:     }
16297:     if (treeGetValue(node)) {
16298:         const queue = repoBuildTransactionQueue(repo, node);
16299:         util.assert(queue.length > 0, 'Sending zero length transaction queue');
16300:         const allRun = queue.every((transaction) => transaction.status === 0 /* TransactionStatus.RUN */);
16301:         // If they're all run (and not sent), we can send them.  Else, we must wait.
16302:         if (allRun) {
16303:             repoSendTransactionQueue(repo, treeGetPath(node), queue);
16304:         }
16305:     }
16306:     else if (treeHasChildren(node)) {
16307:         treeForEachChild(node, childNode => {
16308:             repoSendReadyTransactions(repo, childNode);
16309:         });
16310:     }

00159:  * [DocumentReference]{@link DocumentReference},
00160:  * [WriteBatch]{@link WriteBatch}, [BulkWriter]{@link BulkWriter}, and
00161:  * [Transaction]{@link Transaction}. Using Preconditions, these calls
00162:  * can be restricted to only apply to documents that match the specified
00163:  * conditions.
00164:  *
00165:  * @example
00166:  * ```
00167:  * const documentRef = firestore.doc('coll/doc');
00168:  *
00169:  * documentRef.get().then(snapshot => {
00170:  *   const updateTime = snapshot.updateTime;
00171:  *
00172:  *   console.log(`Deleting document at update time: ${updateTime.toDate()}`);
00173:  *   return documentRef.delete({ lastUpdateTime: updateTime });
00174:  * });
00175:  *

00181:  * or must not exist.

00582: function isRetryableTransactionError(error) {
00583:     if (error.code !== undefined) {
00584:         // This list is based on https://github.com/firebase/firebase-js-sdk/blob/master/packages/firestore/src/core/transaction_runner.ts#L112
00585:         switch (error.code) {
00586:             case 10 /* StatusCode.ABORTED */:
00587:             case 1 /* StatusCode.CANCELLED */:
00588:             case 2 /* StatusCode.UNKNOWN */:
00589:             case 4 /* StatusCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED */:
00590:             case 13 /* StatusCode.INTERNAL */:
00591:             case 14 /* StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE */:
00592:             case 16 /* StatusCode.UNAUTHENTICATED */:
00593:             case 8 /* StatusCode.RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED */:
00594:                 return true;
00595:             case 3 /* StatusCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT */:
00596:                 // The Firestore backend uses "INVALID_ARGUMENT" for transactions
00597:                 // IDs that have expired. While INVALID_ARGUMENT is generally not
00598:                 // retryable, we retry this specific case.
00599:                 return !!error.message.match(/transaction has expired/);
00600:             default:
00601:                 return false;
-------------------------------------------------------------
00579:         }
00580:     }

01189:   /**
01190:    * A write batch, used to perform multiple writes as a single atomic unit.
01191:    *
01192:    * A `WriteBatch` object can be acquired by calling `Firestore.batch()`. It
01193:    * provides methods for adding writes to the write batch. None of the
01194:    * writes will be committed (or visible locally) until `WriteBatch.commit()`
01195:    * is called.
01196:    *
01197:    * Unlike transactions, write batches are persisted offline and therefore are
01198:    * preferable when you don't need to condition your writes on read data.
01199:    */
01200:   export class WriteBatch {
01201:     private constructor();
01202: 
01203:     /**
01204:      * Create the document referred to by the provided `DocumentReference`. The
01205:      * operation will fail the batch if a document exists at the specified
01206:      * location.
01207:      *
-------------------------------------------------------------
01186:     readonly failedAttempts: number;
01187:   }
01188: 
01189:   /**
01190:    * A write batch, used to perform multiple writes as a single atomic unit.
01191:    *
01192:    * A `WriteBatch` object can be acquired by calling `Firestore.batch()`. It
01193:    * provides methods for adding writes to the write batch. None of the
01194:    * writes will be committed (or visible locally) until `WriteBatch.commit()`
01195:    * is called.
01196:    *
01197:    * Unlike transactions, write batches are persisted offline and therefore are
01198:    * preferable when you don't need to condition your writes on read data.
01199:    */

01192:    * A `WriteBatch` object can be acquired by calling `Firestore.batch()`. It

00079: export function callErrorFromStatus(
00080:   status: StatusObject,
00081:   callerStack: string
00082: ): ServiceError {
00083:   const message = `${status.code} ${Status[status.code]}: ${status.details}`;
00084:   const error = new Error(message);
00085:   const stack = `${error.stack}\nfor call at\n${callerStack}`;
00086:   return Object.assign(new Error(message), status, { stack });
00087: }

00010:  * in-process function calls to sub-components. A Trace has a single, top-level
00011:  * "root" Span that in turn may have zero or more child Spans, which in turn
00012:  * may have children.

00093:         // ArrayBuffers are not supported. the binary string fallback, however, is unsafe.
00094:         if (options.binary) {
00095:             var buffer = xhr.response;
00096:             if (!buffer) {
00097:                 buffer = [];
00098:                 for (var i = 0; i < xhr.responseText.length; ++i)
00099:                     buffer.push(xhr.responseText.charCodeAt(i) & 255);
00100:             }
00101:             return callback(null, typeof Uint8Array !== "undefined" ? new Uint8Array(buffer) : buffer);
00102:         }
00103:         return callback(null, xhr.responseText);
00104:     };
00105:

00252:      * Starts asynchronous cancellation on a long-running operation.  The server
00253:      * makes a best effort to cancel the operation, but success is not
00254:      * guaranteed.  If the server doesn't support this method, it returns
00255:      * `google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`.  Clients can use
00256:      * {@link Operations.GetOperation} or
00257:      * other methods to check whether the cancellation succeeded or whether the
00258:      * operation completed despite cancellation. On successful cancellation,
00259:      * the operation is not deleted; instead, it becomes an operation with
00260:      * an {@link Operation.error} value with a {@link google.rpc.Status.code} of
00261:      * 1, corresponding to `Code.CANCELLED`.
00262:      *
00263:      * @param {Object} request - The request object that will be sent.
00264:      * @param {string} request.name - The name of the operation resource to be cancelled.
00265:      * @param {Object=} options
00266:      *   Optional parameters. You can override the default settings for this call,
00267:      * e.g, timeout, retries, paginations, etc. See [gax.CallOptions]{@link
00268:      * https://googleapis.github.io/gax-nodejs/global.html#CallOptions} for the
00269:      * details.
00270:      * @param {function(?Error)=} callback
00271:      *   The function which will be called with the result of the API call.
00272:      * @return {Promise} - The promise which resolves when API call finishes.
00273:      *   The promise has a method named "cancel" which cancels the ongoing API
00274:      * call.
00275:      *

02897:     things, that a prospective certification path (a sequence of n
02898:     certificates or a 'chain') satisfies the following conditions:
02899: 
02900:     (a) for all x in {1, ..., n-1}, the subject of certificate x is
02901:           the issuer of certificate x+1;
02902: 
02903:     (b) certificate 1 is issued by the trust anchor;
02904: 
02905:     (c) certificate n is the certificate to be validated; and
02906: 
02907:     (d) for all x in {1, ..., n}, the certificate was valid at the
02908:           time in question.
02909: 
02910:     Note that here 'n' is index 0 in the chain and 1 is the last certificate
02911:     in the chain and it must be signed by a certificate in the connection's
02912:     CA store.
02913: 
02914:     The path validation process also determines the set of certificate
02915:     policies that are valid for this path, based on the certificate policies

00173: // Validates as many continuation bytes for a multi-byte UTF-8 character as
00174: // needed or are available. If we see a non-continuation byte where we expect
00175: // one, we "replace" the validated continuation bytes we've seen so far with
00176: // a single UTF-8 replacement character ('\ufffd'), to match v8's UTF-8 decoding
00177: // behavior. The continuation byte check is included three times in the case
00178: // where all of the continuation bytes for a character exist in the same buffer.
00179: // It is also done this way as a slight performance increase instead of using a
00180: // loop.
00181: function utf8CheckExtraBytes(self, buf, p) {
00182:   if ((buf[0] & 0xC0) !== 0x80) {
00183:     self.lastNeed = 0;
00184:     return '\ufffd';
00185:   }
00186:   if (self.lastNeed > 1 && buf.length > 1) {
00187:     if ((buf[1] & 0xC0) !== 0x80) {
00188:       self.lastNeed = 1;
00189:       return '\ufffd';
00190:     }

00077: function prizeHash(prizes) {
00078:   const arr = [];
00079:   for (let i = 1; i <= 7; i++) arr.push(prizes?.[i] || "");
00080:   return crypto.createHash("sha1").update(arr.join("|")).digest("hex").slice(0, 12);
00081: }

00087:   return true;

00312:   if (key == null) return;
00313:   const k = String(key);
00314:   const cur = map.get(k) || { count: 0, firstSeen: seq };
00315:   cur.count += 1;

00317:   map.set(k, cur);
